final_candidates.decision_summary: Best combined structural compatibility (0.995) and sequence plausibility (1.000), with no functional annotation conflicts. Retained as top candidate.
Near-perfect structural compatibility (0.985) offsets moderate sequence_plm score; MSA shows the position is highly conserved but buried WT M to L is plausible for packing stability.
Conservative increase in side-chain size with good structural compatibility (0.780) and strong sequence plausibility (0.713), supporting stability while likely preserving entry.

stop_reason.detail: All four tool calls available in this run have been exhausted, and the current top three candidates are stable.

history.rationale: Replacing an oxidation-prone surface methionine with leucine may reduce chemical degradation and improve environmental persistence without substantially perturbing HA1 folding.
Conservative hydrophobic substitution likely to improve core packing with low functional-site risk.
Strong sequence plausibility and moderate evolutionary tolerance, but no structure score available; kept as backup.
Despite high sequence plausibility, lack of structural coverage (app=0.00) makes its folding stability effect too uncertain relative to the top three candidates.

rejection.reason: Despite high sequence plausibility, lack of structural coverage (app=0.00) makes its folding stability effect too uncertain relative to the top three candidates.

history.rationale: M242 is a solvent-accessible methionine; substitution to leucine removes an oxidation liability while preserving hydrophobic character.
M242L is conservative and likely stabilizes hydrophobic packing without disrupting receptor binding or fusion.
Excellent fixed-backbone compatibility supports fold retention, outweighing weak sequence/evolutionary priors.
Retained despite moderate sequence score because structural compatibility is excellent.
M305L is a conservative replacement that may reduce oxidation and improve HA1 stability without affecting receptor binding or fusion motifs.
Conservative substitution near HA1 C-terminus; likely stability benefit with limited cleavage-site interference.
Best joint evidence: neutral ESM-1v score and top ProteinMPNN backbone compatibility; low MSA frequency is tolerable for a stability-engineered substitution.
Retained as top candidate given strong structural compatibility and high sequence plausibility.
Valine at position 150 fills a likely hydrophobic cavity better than alanine, potentially enhancing HA1 core packing and thermostability.
Conservative, but A150 lies in a surface/antigenic loop that may influence receptor binding; lower confidence pending structural evidence.
Poor sequence and strong negative structural compatibility.

rejection.reason: Poor sequence and strong negative structural compatibility.

history.rationale: A389 lies near the HA2 coiled-coil region; increasing side-chain volume to valine may improve hydrophobic core packing and trimer stability.
A389V in HA2 may improve helical packing; conservative and unlikely to block fusion conformational change.
Very low sequence plausibility and no structural support; unlikely to stabilize while preserving entry.

rejection.reason: Very low sequence plausibility and no structural support; unlikely to stabilize while preserving entry.

history.rationale: Replacing a surface-loop glycine with alanine can reduce loop flexibility and increase folding stability while likely preserving function.
Adding a methyl group in the 130-loop could rigidify the loop but risks altering receptor-binding properties.
Poor sequence and negative structural compatibility.

rejection.reason: Poor sequence and negative structural compatibility.

history.rationale: G332 is in a flexible region near the HA1/HA2 boundary; alanine substitution may rigidify the local backbone and improve stability without blocking cleavage.
Near the HA1/HA2 boundary; increased rigidity could affect cleavage or fusion activation, so downweighted.
MSA tolerance is high but structural and sequence-model scores strongly oppose it.

rejection.reason: MSA tolerance is high but structural and sequence-model scores strongly oppose it.

history.rationale: Proline introduction at a turn/loop position can lower configurational entropy and stabilize the native HA1 fold.
Proline in the 130-loop is risky for receptor binding despite possible local stabilization; kept only as a low-priority candidate.
Some evolutionary tolerance but strong negative structural/sequence compatibility.

rejection.reason: Some evolutionary tolerance but strong negative structural/sequence compatibility.

history.rationale: Isoleucine at position 163 is a conservative beta-branched substitution that may improve hydrophobic packing in the HA1 core.
Very conservative hydrophobic change; low expected functional disruption.
Moderate structural compatibility plus good sequence plausibility; conservative I substitution likely preserves function.
Retained with good structural and sequence support.
G392 lies in a HA2 loop outside the fusion peptide; alanine substitution may reduce flexibility and increase overall HA stability while preserving cell entry.
G-to-A can rigidify helical regions, but position is in HA2 and may affect fusion-core dynamics enough to warrant caution.
Negligible sequence plausibility and no coordinates for structural validation.

rejection.reason: Negligible sequence plausibility and no coordinates for structural validation.
